card.title: Speech Pathology
card.description: Support communication, language, speech development and social connection.

sections.title: Speech Pathology
sections.intro: Speech Pathology supports people to communicate more confidently and effectively. Therapy can be tailored around speech sounds, language, fluency, social communication, early communication and participation in everyday conversations.

sections.title: Support built around everyday participation.
sections.intro: Therapy goals are individual. These examples show common areas that may be explored when they are relevant to the person and their priorities.

items.title: Speech sound development
items.description: Support for clearer speech and age-appropriate speech sound development.

items.title: Receptive language
items.description: Understanding words, instructions, questions and everyday language.

items.title: Expressive language
items.description: Building vocabulary, sentences, storytelling and the ability to share ideas.

items.title: Fluency
items.description: Support for stuttering and comfortable, confident communication.

items.title: Social communication
items.description: Conversation, turn-taking, perspective-taking and communication with peers.

items.title: Early communication
items.description: Play-based support for early language, connection and communication development.

panels.title: Goals first, service second.
paragraphs: Speech Pathology can support children and young people across a wide range of communication needs. Service suitability is discussed individually.
We start by understanding what is working well, what feels difficult and what meaningful change would look like in daily life. From there, the clinician can recommend a suitable next step.

items.title: Start with your priorities
items.description: Tell us what matters, what is currently difficult and what you hope to change.

items.title: Understand strengths & needs
items.description: Your clinician gathers relevant information and completes assessment where appropriate.

items.title: Build practical strategies
items.description: Sessions focus on meaningful goals and strategies that make sense in real routines.

items.title: Review & adapt
items.description: Progress is reviewed together and the plan is adjusted as needs and goals change.

sections.title: Before you get started.
sections.intro: These answers are general. We can discuss individual circumstances when you contact the team.

items.question: What happens in the first appointment?
items.answer: The first appointment is usually used to understand communication strengths, concerns, priorities and the environments where support is most needed.

items.question: Is therapy play-based?
items.answer: For many children, play can be an effective and engaging way to build communication skills. The approach is adjusted to the person's age, goals and preferences.

items.question: Can parents and carers be involved?
items.answer: Yes. Family involvement can help strategies transfer into everyday communication and routines.

sections.title: Let’s find the right starting point.
